name: BY ANY OTHER NAME
clue: Constantine renamed Byzantium for himself in 330 A.D.; since 1930 the city bridging the Bosporus has officially used this name

name: MATH IMMORTALS
clue: This prolific Swiss mathematician's famous identity unites e, i, pi, 1 and 0 in a single equation

name: NOBEL PHYSICS
clue: Einstein's 1921 Nobel Prize cited his explanation of this effect, not his theories of relativity

name: DYSTOPIAN TITLES
clue: Ray Bradbury titled this novel after the temperature at which he was told book paper catches fire

name: UNFINISHED BUSINESS
clue: This Austrian composer's Symphony No. 8, left with only two completed movements, is known simply as the 'Unfinished'

name: ONE-BOOK WONDER
clue: Her Pulitzer-winning 1960 story of Scout, Jem & Atticus stood as her only published novel for the next 55 years

name: HIGH FIVES
clue: On April 4, 1964, this band pulled off a Billboard first, holding all 5 of the Hot 100's top 5 positions at once

name: CROWNING MOMENTS
clue: Born in 1769, a year after Genoa ceded his island birthplace to France, he crowned himself emperor in Notre-Dame in 1804

name: POETRY IN MOTION
clue: Baltimore's NFL team takes its name from an 1845 poem by this writer, who died in that city & was buried there in 1849

name: CHAIN REACTIONS
clue: After 1945's Trinity test, this Manhattan Project lab director recalled the Bhagavad Gita: 'Now I am become Death'

name: COLD WAR CHESS
clue: In Reykjavik in 1972, this American ended a 24-year Soviet grip on the world chess championship

name: FOLK HEROES
clue: The 2016 Nobel in Literature went to this Minnesota-born songwriter for 'new poetic expressions within the great American song tradition'

name: FULL CIRCLE
clue: Killed in a Philippine island battle in 1521, he didn't live to complete the first circumnavigation his expedition finished

name: ALOHA MEANS GOODBYE
clue: Deposed in 1893, this last monarch of Hawaii was also a gifted songwriter whose compositions include 'Aloha 'Oe'.

name: PLANETARY NAMES
clue: Alone among the eight planets, this one takes its name from Greek rather than Roman mythology

name: QUIET ON THE SET
clue: This silent-film icon co-founded United Artists in 1919; his 1972 honorary Oscar drew a 12-minute standing ovation

name: CAPITAL NAMESAKES
clue: Liberia's capital city honors this U.S. president, whose namesake doctrine warned European powers away from the Americas

name: MEDICAL IMMORTALITY
clue: Cancer cells taken from this Virginia woman without her consent in 1951 became the first immortal human cell line, called HeLa.

name: ELEMENT OF SURPRISE
clue: Spotted in the Sun's spectrum during an 1868 eclipse and named for a Greek god, it wasn't found on Earth until 1895

name: SHOT IN THE ARM
clue: Noticing that milkmaids who caught cowpox never got smallpox, this Gloucestershire doctor performed the first vaccination in 1796.

name: DRAWN TO GREATNESS
clue: Skeptics dubbed it 'Disney's Folly'; this 1937 feature earned Walt an honorary Oscar — one statuette plus 7 miniatures

name: EUROPEAN RIVERS
clue: Rising in Germany's Black Forest, this river touches 10 countries on its way to the sea — more than any other river on Earth

name: CURRENT AFFAIRS
clue: After quizzing his whaling-captain cousin, Benjamin Franklin published one of the first charts of this warm Atlantic current.

name: MEMORY LANE
clue: Andrew Lloyd Webber set T.S. Eliot's playful 1939 verse collection to music in this show, once Broadway's longest-running

name: FOILED AGAIN!
clue: Once so costly it was displayed beside France's crown jewels, this lightweight metal crowned the Washington Monument in 1884

name: WORLD WAR II
clue: Clouds over the primary target of Kokura diverted the second atomic bomb to this city in August 1945

name: HOMESICK HARMONIES
clue: While running a New York conservatory, this Bohemian composer poured spirituals and prairie summers into his symphony 'From the New World'.

name: DAYS OF THE WEEK
clue: Thursday belongs to the thunder god Thor; this day of the week honors his one-eyed father

name: WORLD CUP HISTORY
clue: In 1930 this nation of some 2 million people hosted the first FIFA World Cup and won it too

name: PERFECT SEASONS
clue: The 1972 edition of this NFL team went 17-0, the league's only unbeaten season capped by a Super Bowl win
